data.text/markdown:
Rigid transformations from point correspondences

Given pairs of corresponding points measured in two frames, which rigid transformation (rotation plus translation) best maps one set onto the other? This problem is at the core of landmark-based localization, point-cloud registration and camera pose estimation. This notebook uses the MRPT Python wheel (pip install mrpt3) to solve it in 2D and 3D, with the mrpt.tfest module:
  • se2_l2: closed-form least-squares SE(2) solution.
  • se3_l2_robust: RANSAC around Horn's closed-form SE(3) solution.
plus mrpt.poses (CPose2D, CPose3D, CPose3DQuat) for the poses. Real correspondences are noisy, and some are plain wrong (outliers). Move the sliders: a few outliers are enough to ruin least squares, while RANSAC ignores them, up to a point.

data.text/markdown:
How the estimators work

Each correspondence pairs a point ||(p_i||) measured in the sensor (local) frame with a point ||(g_i||) in the map (global) frame. The transformation ||(T||) we look for satisfies ||(g_i \approx T \oplus p_i||).
  • Least squares minimizes ||(\sum_i \lVert g_i - T \oplus p_i \rVert^2||) in closed form. Fast and optimal for Gaussian noise, but one wrong pair far away pulls the whole solution.
  • RANSAC repeatedly fits ||(T||) to 5 random pairs, collects the pairs that agree with it (adding one moves the fitted pose by less than the threshold, and rotates it less than 1°), and keeps the largest consensus set. It succeeds if at least one random 5-pair sample has no outliers.

1. SE(2): robot pose from landmarks

A robot observes landmarks whose positions in the map are known. Each observation, in the robot frame, is matched to a map landmark, and some matches are wrong. The transformation from robot to map frame is the robot pose ||((x, y, \phi)||). For RANSAC we use se3_l2_robust with all ||(z = 0||): a planar problem is a special case of SE(3).

Method Translation error (cm) Rotation error (deg) Pairs used Outliers among them
Least squares (se2_l2) 50.5 0.60 60 18
RANSAC (se3_l2_robust) 0.1 0.01 42 0
True outliers: 18 of 60. Chance that one of the 200 RANSAC samples is outlier-free: 100.0%.

2. SE(3): pose of a 3D sensor

A 3D sensor sees points on the faces of a box-shaped object whose model is known, and each sensed point is matched to a model point. Now the transformation has six degrees of freedom. Drag the 3D views to rotate them: with outliers, the least-squares fit leaves the sensed points (colored) visibly off the model (gray).

Method Translation error (cm) Rotation error (deg) Pairs used Outliers among them
Least squares (Horn) 18.9 3.56 60 18
RANSAC (se3_l2_robust) 0.9 0.26 42 0

Things to try
  • Set the outlier ratio to 0: both methods agree, and their error grows with the noise.
  • Raise the outlier ratio: least squares degrades at once, RANSAC keeps working until the outlier-free chance (above) drops, or until fewer than 25% of the pairs are inliers, the smallest consensus set accepted here.
  • With large noise, a small threshold makes RANSAC reject good pairs too.

Run it on your computer (Linux, Python 3.11 to 3.14): 
uvx marimo edit --sandbox https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MRPT/mrpt-notebooks/main/notebooks/rigid_transform_estimation.py
